newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-ENGLISH CLUBS FACE MORE UPHEAVAL.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-ENGLISH CLUBS FACE MORE UPHEAVAL.

text.p: English club rugby is facing a summer of continued strife at home as its top players fly out to face opponents in South Africa, Australia and Argentina.

The sacking of former England coach Dick Best as Harlequins supremo on Tuesday has highlighted the increasingly dark side of the modern professional game in a week of renewed hostilities between rival factions at Twickenham.
The Rugby Football Union (RFU) came under more fire on Wednesday from a group headed by British Lions manager Fran Cotton who claim senior officials are running the union "undemocratically."

The RFU Reform Group are backing executive committee chairman Cliff Brittle in forthcoming elections for a restructured management board, and are putting mounting pressure on RFU secretary Tony Hallett.
It seems likely that one of the two men will be forced to step down in the coming months, adding to English game's lengthening list of prominent casualties since professionalism arrived.

Best's sacking at Quins after 23 service with the London club, amid criticism of a man-management style which long ago earned him the nickname "Sulphuric", mirrors recent upheavals at rivals Bath and Leicester.

Jon Hall and Brian Ashton both left Bath in mid-season and Leicester's former Wallaby coach Bob Dwyer was only installed as director of rugby after his long-time predecessor Tony Russ was unceremoniously dumped a year ago.
Just three of the 12 first division clubs are likely to start next season with the same coach/director of rugby they had a year ago, with long service in the amateur era seemingly a disadvantage.

It certainly increases the pressure on the likes of Francois Pienaar and Rob Andrew, for whom lofty player/coach reputations will not be enough if results are disappointing at Saracens and Newcastle next season.

"The stress has increased enormously since the game went professional because there is so much more at stake," said Hall, who has not been able to bring himself to watch a game at Bath since his February exit.
"The one certainty is that it will get more stressful and next season more coaches will get the sack."
Quins have already been linked with All Black number eight Zinzan Brooke, unless the club's backers try to tempt former England captain Will Carling to take a more prominent role at his own club.
There are also certain to be renewed attempts from several clubs to lure more overseas signings, some of whom stand to gain handsome rewards if they impress English opponents in the next few weeks.
There are 18 Englishmen on the British Lions tour of South Africa, and England will also play a test in Australia in July following a six-match visit to Argentina.
